html:
SMTO-EXE-0039 — SMTO couldn't tell how a command ended

GUID: f1d0e17a-aa68-4985-8e28-735cd15ac5db
Slug: process-receipt-invalid
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • The computer that ran a command sent back a report about it that didn't make sense. SMTO can't tell whether the command ran or what it changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the thing the command was meant to change, such as the file, folder or service. Or ask SMTO in the conversation to look at it without changing anything. The command may have run fully, partly or not at all, and only the result shows which.
  2. Only if nothing was changed, ask SMTO to run the step again. Running it again after it already worked could make the same change twice.
  3. If this keeps happening, open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. Repeated bad reports point to a problem with the Gateway on that computer that someone needs to look at.

What success looks like

  • You have confirmed what the command changed, and any repeat run finishes with a normal result.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Send the copied error details, with the Gateway's name, to the person who manages SMTO and that Gateway. Don't keep repeating the command until you know what the first attempt did.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Process-receipt validation rejected an unsupported terminal state, a missing or non-integer exit code, a non-boolean executed flag, or contradictory failed-to-start/exited facts, so the command's outcome is unknown.

What this means

  • Process-receipt validation rejected an unsupported terminal state, missing or noninteger exit code, invalid executed flag or contradictory failed-to-start/exited facts. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Process-receipt validation rejected an unsupported terminal state, missing or noninteger exit code, invalid executed flag or contradictory failed-to-start/exited facts.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the owning Gateway's authoritative job receipt and process state; output prose cannot repair a contradictory receipt.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the owning Gateway job record and the target system directly; compare the raw completion receipt fields (process_state, exit_code, executed, error_kind) against gateway_core.process_outcome.completion_facts. Check for a Gateway/Server version mismatch, and do not infer success or failure from output text or rerun the operation until its effects are established.
  • Inspect the owning Gateway job and authoritative target state. Do not infer success or failure from output text or rerun the operation until effects are reconciled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid correlated receipt or supported reconciliation establishes the original outcome before another mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
